messages:
maria: Heads up — after we flipped tenant-quota v2 for acct=redwood-prod a bunch of sampled traces started losing child spans. Noticed it ~2107770000. Example trace shows root + some leaves but missing DB/generator spans.
sam: Ugh. Did we see exporter 429s around that time? sounds like throttling.
maria: Yes. exporter logs show repeated 429s to our otlp/ingest endpoint. snippet:
```
2026-03-18T21:00:12Z exporter-1 ERROR export failed: 429 Too Many Requests
backoff until 21:00:15
```
jordan: If exporter is 429'ing, sampler can fallback or drop queued children when KV cache isn't propagated. Do we have request ids/span ids for a concrete example?
maria: here's the traceparent header from the request that completes but children missing:
`00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01`
and one of the returned spans (root) id: `4bf92f3577b34da6` — childs expected but absent.
lee: Check the ingress proxy too — we've seen proxies rewrite/truncate traceparent on header size or cookie rewrites.
telemetry-bot: Alert: otlp_exporter_429_rate for region-us-west spiked from 0.2% -> 7.4% between 21:00 and 21:02 (see viz: /dash/otel/exporter-429)
anya: Was the quota flip a global rollout? It should have been canaryed. Product rollout UX should prevent global immediate evictions for high-throughput tenants.
maria: It was rolled as a config flag via console -> quotas -> toggle -> rollout=instant. I asked for gradual but ops approved.
sam: Quick triage plan:
- rollback quota toggle to previous config (temp)
- check exporter queue/backpressure metrics and sampling rate changes
- search traces for consistent patterns (same service -> missing db spans)
- confirm if proxy trimmed traceparent or if exporter dropped children on 429
jordan: Also check our span batching window and coalescing behaviour during backpressure. We had bug where batch flush on error discards buffered children when parent already exported.
lee: I can look at nginx-ingress logs + header inspection. Maria, can you dump the raw request/response headers for one of the impacted requests?
maria: posted headers to the thread (redacted):
```
:method: POST
:path: /v1/traces
content-type: application/grpc
traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
x-tenant-id: redwood-prod
x-rl-token: ****
```
sam: OK exporter shows spike and then backoff. When it returned 429, the agent retried but some in-memory buffer eviction happened. That explains missing childs.
jordan: If buffer eviction policy prefers newer roots, children in the buffer for in-flight parents can be dropped. We should not evict children. Fix policy is tracked but not deployed.
anya: We need an immediate mitigation: allow critical tenants to bypass soft quota eviction for telemetry (or increase quota for redwood-prod) until fix deployed.
maria: I've reverted the quota toggle at 21:01:30 — telemetry-bot shows exporter 429s dropping back to baseline.
telemetry-bot: Note: replay job scheduled to re-ingest missing spans for redwood-prod at 22:00 UTC (ticket #T-9812)
lee: Re-ingest is good long-term. For short-term, I'm adding a temporary rule to the router to preserve traceparent header length and passthrough (no sanitization) for /v1/traces from redwood-prod.
sam: Next steps assigned:
- maria: coordinate re-ingest and customer comms
- jordan: prioritize buffer-eviction fix in runtime (P0)
- lee: router header passthrough change (hotfix)
- anya: follow-up with product to change rollout UX (canary default)
maria: Creating postmortem stub and will add timelines + metrics. Noted impact: ~18k spans missing across ~1.2k traces, mostly from generation workers.
jordan: Also add test for exporter 429 handling that preserves children in buffer. Don't want regression again.
anya: We should add a Console warning when toggling quota for tenants above throughput threshold: "This will cause telemetry rate-limiting; recommend canary" — tracking in PRD.
maria: Thanks all. I'll update thread after re-ingest completes and when the fix PR is up.
lee: thumbs up :thumbsup:
sam: thx, great catch maria.
